models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.notes: Strongest model under 10B (AA Index 32). Gated DeltaNet hybrid, so KV cache stays small. Native image/video input. Thinking is on by default and answers are token-heavy. Total is 9.65B incl. vision encoder (8.95B text).

models.name: Qwen3.5 4B
models.notes: Best 4B-class model (AA Index 27) and a good default for laptops. Hybrid thinking, native vision, 262K context.

models.name: Qwen3.5 2B
models.notes: Phone-class multimodal model with hybrid thinking. Linear attention keeps long-context memory low.

models.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B
models.notes: Tiny multimodal model for phones and browsers. Fine for simple tasks, weak on knowledge.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.notes: Takes text, image and audio input. 4.5B effective params, 8B with per-layer embeddings. Strong generalist for 8-16GB machines. Ollama q4 download is 9.6GB (6.1GB for the QAT tag).

models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.notes: 2.3B effective params, with audio and vision input. Built for phones. Ollama q4 download is 7.2GB (4.3GB for the QAT tag).

models.name: MiniCPM5 2B
models.notes: Released Sept 2026. Dense Llama-architecture model with hybrid thinking. Claims 2B-class SOTA over Qwen3.5-2B, Gemma 4 E2B and LFM2.5-2.6B.

models.name: Granite 4.2 8B
models.notes: Native thinking with full, off and low-effort modes. Strong tool calling and RAG. Supersedes Granite 4.1 (Apr 2026).

models.name: Granite 4.2 3B
models.notes: Compact enterprise reasoning and tool-calling model with switchable thinking.

models.name: Ornith 1.5 9B
models.notes: Self-improving agentic coding model built on Qwen3.5-9B, with image input. Very popular for local coding agents (GGUF has about 5M downloads). Thinking is on by default.

models.name: Ling 3.0 Tiny (7.9B-A1.3B)
models.notes: MoE with hybrid KDA+MLA attention, so it decodes fast on CPU and Mac. Thinking is on by default. Runs as GGUF (bartowski) in llama.cpp and LM Studio. Ollama support is currently limited to an MLX PR.

models.name: LFM2.5 2.6B
models.in_browser: transformers.js ONNX WebGPU (LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-ONNX; official WebGPU demo)
models.notes: Hybrid conv+attention. Very fast on CPU (113 tok/s on a Ryzen) in under 2.5GB. Good for agents, tools and RAG. Not recommended for coding.

models.name: Nanbeige4.2 3B
models.notes: Looped transformer with 3B non-embedding params. Tops AA's phone leaderboard, but decodes slower than its size suggests. Needs Nanbeige's llama.cpp fork.

models.name: LFM2.5 8B-A1B
models.notes: On-device MoE with 1.5B active params. About 30 tok/s on an iPhone and 253 tok/s on an M5 Max, in under 6GB. Built for tool calling.

models.name: MiniCPM5 1B
models.notes: 1B model with hybrid think/no-think. Scores 45 on AA's phone index, strong for a 1B.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Nano 4B
models.notes: Mamba-2 hybrid with only 4 attention layers, pruned from Nemotron Nano 9B v2. Reasoning can be toggled. Aimed at edge agents.

models.name: LFM2.5 350M
models.notes: Ultra-small model for extraction and classification. Runs on almost anything, including the browser.

models.name: LFM2.5 1.2B (Instruct / Thinking)
models.notes: Runs in under 1GB at about 70 tok/s on a Galaxy S25 CPU. Instruct is available via hf.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-GGUF. The card lists 32K context, but Ollama shows 125K for the Thinking build.

models.name: Ministral 3 8B
models.notes: 8.4B language model plus 0.4B vision encoder, with image input. Comes in Instruct, Reasoning and Base variants. Native function calling.

models.name: Ministral 3 3B
models.notes: Edge model with vision input. Reasoning variant also available. Supported in WebLLM.

models.name: OLMo 3 7B (Instruct / Think)
models.notes: Fully open: data, code and checkpoints. Think variant is olmo-3:7b-think. Full multi-head attention means a large KV cache (~2GB at 4K context).

models.name: Qwen3-VL 8B Instruct
models.notes: Most-downloaded small VLM (about 17M/month): OCR, GUI and video. Vision projector adds 1.16GB. Thinking variants exist. For chat, Qwen3.5-9B largely supersedes it.

models.name: Qwen3-VL 4B Instruct
models.notes: Compact VLM for OCR and screenshots. Vision projector adds 0.84GB. A 2B sibling is also available (qwen3-vl:2b).

models.name: Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507
models.in_browser: transformers.js ONNX (onnx-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-ONNX); WebLLM only has the original Qwen3-4B-q4f16_1-MLC (~3.4GB VRAM)
models.notes: Non-thinking update of Qwen3 4B with 256K context. Still very popular (about 4M downloads/month).

models.name: Qwen3 4B Thinking 2507
models.notes: Reasoning-only 4B, strong at math and code. Long chains of thought make it slow on weak hardware.

models.name: Gemma 3 270M
models.notes: Tiny base for task-specific fine-tuning. Not a capable general chat model.

models.name: SmolLM3 3B
models.notes: Fully open recipe, dual-mode reasoning, 6 languages. Context extends to 128K with YaRN. No official Ollama library entry.

models.name: Gemma 3n E4B
models.notes: Superseded by Gemma 4 E4B. Mobile-first MatFormer with per-layer embeddings, taking audio and vision input. Ollama download is 7.5GB.

models.name: Gemma 3n E2B
models.notes: Superseded by Gemma 4 E2B. Phone-first model. Ollama download is 5.6GB.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
models.notes: R1-0528 chain of thought distilled into Qwen3-8B. It is the default deepseek-r1:8b tag in Ollama. Very verbose reasoning.

models.name: Phi-4-mini-reasoning 3.8B
models.notes: Math-focused reasoning model, not meant for general chat. No Phi-5 has been released.

models.name: Qwen3 8B
models.notes: Hybrid thinking with a huge fine-tune ecosystem (about 12M downloads/month). Qwen3.5-9B largely supersedes it. Native context is 32K, 128K with YaRN.

models.name: Qwen3 1.7B
models.notes: Small hybrid-thinking model, common on phones and in browsers.

models.name: Qwen3 0.6B
models.notes: Most-downloaded tiny LLM (about 30M/month). Browser-friendly but limited quality.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B
models.notes: Image input and 140+ languages. Vision projector adds 0.85GB and the Ollama download is 3.3GB. Superseded by Gemma 4 E4B but still very popular.

models.name: Gemma 3 1B
models.notes: Text-only and very popular for phones and browsers (about 3M downloads/month).

models.name: Phi-4-mini-instruct 3.8B
models.notes: Good logic and math for its size, with function calling. Weaker on world knowledge.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 7B
models.notes: Original R1 distill, strong at math and code reasoning but poor at casual chat. Superseded by the 0528-Qwen3-8B distill.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama 8B
models.notes: R1 reasoning distilled into Llama 3.1 8B. The Ollama deepseek-r1:8b tag now points to the Qwen3 distill instead.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B
models.notes: Tiny reasoning model, decent at math and weak at everything else. Popular demo model.

models.name: SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct
models.notes: Older small model, still common in browser demos. Uses full multi-head attention (larger KV cache) and only 8K context.

models.name: SmolLM2 360M Instruct
models.notes: Runs on nearly any device or browser. Only useful for very simple tasks.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct
models.notes: Still the go-to small local coder for chat and fill-in-the-middle. There is no Qwen3-Coder under 30B.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B Instruct
models.notes: Popular tab-autocomplete (fill-in-the-middle) model for Continue and Tabby.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
models.notes: Ubiquitous default small model. Newer 3-4B models beat it, but no newer small Llama exists.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
models.notes: Very popular phone and browser model (about 7.5M downloads/month). Basic quality.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
models.notes: Classic 8B baseline and still ubiquitous. Newer models outclass it. Meta has no small Llama 4/5 (Muse Glimmer is 30B).

models.name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3
models.notes: Legacy but still widely pulled. Superseded by Ministral 3 8B.

notes:
48 entries, newest first. They were checked on 2026-09-29 against the Hugging Face API and file trees, Ollama library tag pages, the WebLLM prebuilt config (mlc-ai/web-llm src/config.ts) and the onnx-community / LiquidAI ONNX repos.

How the fields were filled:
- **Sizes:** q4_gb, q8_gb and fp16_gb are actual GGUF file sizes in decimal GB (Q4_K_M, Q8_0, BF16/F16). They come from unsloth, bartowski or the official GGUF repos, so none needed the formula.
  - For multimodal models the sizes cover the text weights only. The vision projector (mmproj) adds about 0.8-1.2 GB when images are used.
  - Ollama download sizes can differ a lot, especially for Gemma 3n and Gemma 4 E-models, where Ollama bundles the vision/audio towers and heavier embeddings: gemma4:e4b is 9.6GB against a 4.98GB GGUF, and gemma4:e2b is 7.2GB against 3.11GB.
- **params_total_b:** the full checkpoint count from the HF safetensors, including vision and audio encoders. That is why Qwen3.5 9B and Ornith 1.5 9B show 9.65B (8.95B text) and sit just over the 9B line.
- **params_active_b:** equals the total for dense models. For MoE it is the per-token active count (LFM2.5-8B-A1B 1.5B, Ling-3.0-tiny 1.3B). For Gemma 3n and Gemma 4 E-models I used Google's "effective" count (2B/4B and 2.3B/4.5B), because per-layer embeddings are lookups that can be offloaded rather than compute.
- **min_runtime_mem_gb:** Q4_K_M file + fp16 KV cache at 4K context + about 0.3-0.5 GB of runtime buffers. Where WebLLM publishes vram_required_MB, I cross-checked against it.
  - Hybrid linear-attention and SSM models (Qwen3.5, LFM2.5, Nemotron 3 Nano, Ling 3.0) grow their KV cache very little with context.
  - OLMo 3 7B and SmolLM2 use full multi-head attention, so their KV cache is large.
  - Reasoning and thinking-by-default models (Qwen3.5, R1 distills, Ornith, Ling, the Qwen3 Thinking variant) produce long outputs. They feel slow on weak hardware even when they fit in memory.
- **context_k:** native context in K tokens (262144 = 256). YaRN extensions are mentioned in the notes.
- **ollama_tag:** the official library tag where one exists. Otherwise it is an `hf.co/<repo>` tag, which works with `ollama run hf.co/...`. It is empty when Ollama cannot run the model today: Nanbeige needs its own llama.cpp fork, and Ling-3.0-tiny has only an MLX-only Ollama PR, though its GGUF works in llama.cpp and LM Studio.
- **in_browser:** only WebLLM model IDs (with VRAM) and ONNX repos I confirmed exist.

What does and doesn't exist at this tier as of 2026-09-29:
- **OpenAI:** no open-weight model at or under 9B. gpt-oss-20b is 21B total / 3.6B active and belongs to the next tier.
- **Meta:** no small Llama 4 or Llama 5. Its newest open release is Muse Glimmer 30B (Aug 2026).
- **Microsoft:** Phi-5 is only a rumor. The newest small Phi models are Phi-4-mini and Phi-4-mini-reasoning (Phi-4-reasoning-vision is 15B).
- **Apple:** no new open-weight LLM.
- **Qwen:** Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.8 ship only 27B and larger models, so the Qwen3.5 small series (0.8B/2B/4B/9B, Mar 2026) is the newest small Qwen.
- **Google:** Gemma 4 comes as E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B and 31B. The 12B (7.6GB q4 in Ollama) is just above this tier.

Superseded models left out: Granite 4.1 and 4.0 (replaced by Granite 4.2, Aug 2026), LFM2 (replaced by LFM2.5), Qwen2.5 general models, Ministral 8B 2410 and Phi-3.5.

Low-download community fine-tunes seen on HF were left out as too obscure: MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, NeoHorse, K2-Horizon, Spark-X2.5 and Apertus 8B.

Licenses: Gemma 3 and 3n use the Gemma Terms of Use, while Gemma 4 is Apache-2.0. LFM2.5 uses the LFM Open License v1.0, which has a revenue threshold for commercial use. Nemotron uses the NVIDIA Open Model License.
